_doc: POST /v1/connect/requests with purpose sdk_key (docs/plans/onboarding-v2-connect-flow.md section 13.2). request.body is what setup sends (the SDKs build it; the field rules are request_rules). responses are what the cloud answers (internal/cloudserver/api must produce these shapes exactly: the same keys, the same types; ids, codes and times are examples). Cloud errors are the service's usual {error: <message>, code: <code>}; setup decides on code and status only. A purpose sdk_key body never carries device_public_key, and a machine body never carries redeem_hash (400 bad_request either way).

request_rules.purpose: sdk_key (absent or machine: the machine flow of section 2)
request_rules.client: superbased-sdk-python or superbased-sdk-typescript (closed; the package that runs setup)
request_rules.client_version: 1 to 32 of [0-9A-Za-z.+_-]: the SDK package version
request_rules.project_name: 1 to 64 of [a-z0-9._-]: the service name setup detected (the sdk-api-surface.md service-name ladder, normalised); shown on the approval page
request_rules.machine_name: 1 to 64 characters after trimming, control and bidi characters removed (the machine flow's rule); the host name
request_rules.os: 1 to 16 of [a-z0-9_]: Python sys.platform, Node process.platform (linux, darwin, win32)
request_rules.arch: 1 to 16 of [a-z0-9_], lowercased: Python platform.machine().lower(), Node process.arch
request_rules.target_hint: "" or a team slug shape (the machine flow's rule); setup --team <slug>
request_rules.redeem_hash: 43 characters of unpadded base64url: base64url-nopad(SHA-256(ASCII bytes of redeem_secret)); redeem_secret is 32 random bytes as unpadded base64url, kept in memory only (internal/sdkkeygrant RedeemHash, testdata/vectors.json redeem)
